from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        wing_l.next_to(body, LEFT, buff=-0.1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Visualizing Conditional Probability"
        lines = [
            "- Imagine the total sample space is a rectangle.",
            "- Knowing event B occurred shrinks our entire universe.",
            "- The new universe is just the area of B.",
            "- We look only at A's intersection with B.",
            "- This restricted area defines the new conditional probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a large white rectangle (#FFFFFF) representing the total Sample Space.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Rect area B1 to E6 (4 rows high, 6 cols wide)
        sample_space = Rectangle(width=6.0, height=4.0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(sample_space, "B1", "E6")
        
        ss_label = Text("S", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ss_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        ss_label.shift(UP*0.4 + LEFT*0.4)
        
        self.play(Create(sample_space), Write(ss_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Introduce two overlapping circles A (#FF00FF) and B (#00FFFF) inside the rectangle.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        circle_a = Circle(radius=1.2, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=3)
        circle_b = Circle(radius=1.2, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(circle_a, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(circle_b, "C4")
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF")
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "B4")
        label_a.shift(UP*0.5)
        label_b.shift(UP*0.5)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(circle_a), FadeIn(circle_b),
            Write(label_a), Write(label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Darken the entire rectangle except for circle B, showing the "Shrinking Universe".
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dark overlay with a hole for B
        dark_overlay = Rectangle(width=6.0, height=4.0, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(dark_overlay, "B1", "E6")
        universe_mask = Cutout(dark_overlay, circle_b, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLACK, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(universe_mask))
        self.play(
            sample_space.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2),
            ss_label.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.2),
            circle_a.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2).set_fill(opacity=0.1),
            label_a.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight the intersection area (A \cap B) with a bright yellow pulse (#FFFF00).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        intersection = Intersection(circle_a, circle_b, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_width=4)
        self.play(FadeIn(intersection))
        self.play(Indicate(intersection, color="#FFFF00", scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Place a panda icon (#FFFFFF) within the intersection to represent the conditional event.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Text label as panda icon
        panda_icon = Text("Panda", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(panda_icon, "C3", "C4")
        
        self.play(Write(panda_icon))
        self.play(panda_icon.animate.scale(1.2), rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(3)

        # Final cleanup
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Deriving Bayes' Theorem: The Bridge", [
            "The intersection probability can be calculated two ways.",
            "It equals P(A given B) times P(B).",
            "It also equals P(B given A) times P(A).",
            "Equating these gives us the core of Bayes' theorem.",
            "We isolate P(A given B) to find the posterior."
        ])
        
        # Define colors as per requirements
        COLOR_A = "#00FF00"      # P(A) green
        COLOR_BA = "#0000FF"     # P(B|A) blue
        COLOR_AB = "#FF0000"     # P(A|B) red
        COLOR_B = "#FFFFFF"      # P(B) white
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"   # For the glowing box
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Initial intersection equation: P(A \cap B) = P(A|B)P(B)
        eq1 = MathTex("P(A \\cap B)", "=", "P(A|B)", "P(B)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eq1, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Highlight the conditional expansion part P(A|B)P(B)
        rect1 = SurroundingRectangle(eq1[2:], color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect1))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Second intersection equation: P(A \cap B) = P(B|A)P(A)
        eq2 = MathTex("P(A \\cap B)", "=", "P(B|A)", "P(A)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eq2, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(eq2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD))
        # Equate the two right sides: P(A|B)P(B) = P(B|A)P(A)
        eq3 = MathTex("P(A|B)", "P(B)", "=", "P(B|A)", "P(A)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eq3, "D2", "D5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Show derivation from existing equations
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(eq1[2:].copy(), eq3[0:2]),
            ReplacementTransform(eq2[2:].copy(), eq3[3:5]),
            Write(eq3[2])
        )
        
        # Glowing box around the core equivalence
        box = SurroundingRectangle(eq3, color=COLOR_GOLD, buff=0.15)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Use Red color to match the Posterior P(A|B)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_AB))
        
        # Final formula: P(A|B) = (P(B|A)P(A)) / P(B)
        final_eq = MathTex("P(A|B)", "=", "{ P(B|A)", "P(A)", "\\over", "P(B) }", color=WHITE)
        
        # Apply colors to specific terms as per storyboard
        final_eq[0].set_color(COLOR_AB) # Posterior
        final_eq[2].set_color(COLOR_BA) # Likelihood
        final_eq[3].set_color(COLOR_A)  # Prior
        
        self.place_in_area(final_eq, "E2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Clean up derivations and show isolated formula
        self.play(
            FadeOut(box),
            FadeOut(eq1),
            FadeOut(eq2),
            ReplacementTransform(eq3, final_eq)
        )
        
        # Labels for the terms
        label_post = Text("Posterior", font_size=18, color=COLOR_AB)
        label_lik = Text("Likelihood", font_size=18, color=COLOR_BA)
        label_prior = Text("Prior", font_size=18, color=COLOR_A)
        
        # Position labels below their respective parts in the equation
        self.place_at_grid(label_post, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Turn 1 robot icon bright red (#FF0000) to signify the "Broken" prior.

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        broken_robot = robots[0]
        self.play(broken_robot.animate.set_color("#FF0000").scale(1.5))
        self.play(broken_robot.animate.scale(1/1.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate a yellow sensor beam (#FFFF00) scanning a healthy robot and triggering a "Beep".
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Target a healthy robot (index 55)

        scanner = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.3, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.3)

        self.place_at_grid(beep_label, "D5", scale_factor=0.8) # Near the center of the grid area

        calc_text = MathTex(

            font_size=24, color=WHITE

        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(3)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout
        title_text = "Summary: Thinking Like a Bayesian"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Independence ignores evidence; dependence requires updating.",
            "Bayes' theorem provides the mathematical engine for updates.",
            "Use data to move from uncertainty to truth."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors for lecture steps
        color_step1 = BLUE_C
        color_step2 = GREEN_C
        color_step3 = YELLOW_C

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_step1))
        
        # Elements for the flow diagram
        initial_belief = Text("Initial Belief", font_size=20, color=color_step1)
        plus_sign = Text("+", font_size=30, color=WHITE)
        new_data = Text("New Data", font_size=20, color=color_step1)
        flow_arrow = Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        refined_truth = Text("Refined Truth", font_size=20, color=color_step1)
        
        # Positioning using grid
        self.place_at_grid(initial_belief, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(plus_sign, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(new_data, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(flow_arrow, "A5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(refined_truth, "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        flow_diagram = VGroup(initial_belief, plus_sign, new_data, flow_arrow, refined_truth)
        self.play(FadeIn(flow_diagram))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_step2)
        )
        
        # Gauge Visual
        gauge_arc = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI, angle=-PI, color=WHITE)
        # Position gauge in area D2-F5
        self.place_in_area(gauge_arc, "D2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        gauge_center = gauge_arc.get_center()
        
        # Labels for the gauge
        label_uncertain = Text("Uncertain", font_size=16, color=RED).next_to(gauge_arc.get_start(), DOWN)
        label_certain = Text("Certainty", font_size=16, color=GREEN).next_to(gauge_arc.get_end(), DOWN)
        
        # ValueTracker for the needle angle (PI = left/Uncertain, 0 = right/Certainty)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(PI)
        
        # Needle using Arrow for automatic tip handling
        needle = Arrow(gauge_center, gauge_center + LEFT * 1.2, color=color_step2, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        
        def needle_updater(mob):
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            end_point = gauge_center + np.array([1.2 * np.cos(angle), 1.2 * np.sin(angle), 0])
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(gauge_center, end_point)
            
        needle.add_updater(needle_updater)
        
        self.play(Create(gauge_arc), FadeIn(label_uncertain), FadeIn(label_certain), Create(needle))
        
        # Clues that cause updates
        clue_1 = Text("Clue: Fingerprints Found", font_size=18, color=color_step2)
        self.place_at_grid(clue_1, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(clue_1))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI * 0.7), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)

        clue_2 = Text("Clue: Alibi Disproven", font_size=18, color=color_step2)
        self.place_at_grid(clue_2, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(clue_2))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI * 0.3), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_step3)
        )
        
        # Final update to Certainty
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Final Message: "Think Bayesian" (#FFFF00)
        final_message = Text("Think Bayesian", font_size=40, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(final_message, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(final_message))
        self.play(final_message.animate.scale(1.3), rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and the Logic of Independence
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with basic algebra knowledge.

sections.title: The Hook: The Detective's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'updating beliefs' based on new evidence. Explain that probability isn't just about static odds, but a dynamic tool for reasoning. Set the stage for the difference between events that influence each other and those that don't.
sections.example: A rare blue butterfly is spotted in a garden. If we know it's a rainy day, does that change the probability of seeing it? This introduces the intuitive seed of conditional probability.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Independence vs. Dependence
sections.content: Define Independence: Event A does not change the probability of Event B ($P(A|B) = P(A)$). Use a 'Split-Screen' visual: one side showing independent coin tosses, the other showing drawing colored marbles without replacement.
sections.example: Rolling a 6 on a die (Event A) and then flipping a Head (Event B) are independent. But 'It is cloudy' (Event A) and 'It will rain' (Event B) are dependent.

sections.title: Visualizing Conditional Probability
sections.content: Introduce the 'Sample Space Slicer.' Use a Venn Diagram where the total area is 1. Show how 'knowing B has occurred' shrinks the universe from the whole rectangle to only the circle of B. The probability of A is now restricted to the intersection area.
sections.example: Imagine a zoo of 100 animals. 20 are pandas. If I tell you the animal is 'eating bamboo' (the new universe), the probability it's a panda suddenly shoots up.

sections.title: Deriving Bayes' Theorem: The Bridge
sections.content: Show the mathematical bridge: $P(A \cap B) = P(A|B)P(B) = P(B|A)P(A)$. Rearrange this visually to isolate $P(A|B)$. This explains *why* the formula exists rather than just memorizing it. Highlight terms: Prior, Likelihood, and Posterior.
sections.example: Using a tree diagram to show how a path (Prior $\times$ Likelihood) leads to an outcome, then 'reversing' the tree to find the probability of the starting branch.

sections.title: The 'Sick Robot' Case Study
sections.content: A comprehensive example applying the formula. Calculate the 'False Positive' paradox. Use an infographic style: 1,000 robots, 10 are actually broken (Prior), a sensor that is 90% accurate (Likelihood). Calculate the probability a robot is actually broken if the sensor beeps.
sections.example: Even if the sensor beeps (Evidence), if the failure rate is very low (Prior), the robot is likely still fine. This demonstrates why Bayes is vital for medical tests and AI diagnostics.

sections.title: Summary: Thinking Like a Bayesian
sections.content: Recap: 1. Independence means evidence is irrelevant. 2. Dependence means we must update. 3. Bayes' Theorem is the mathematical engine for that update. End with a visual flow: Initial Belief + New Data = Refined Truth.
sections.example: A character 'Detective Bayes' updates his 'Suspect Meter' as new clues (fingerprints vs. weather) are found, moving from uncertainty to high-probability conclusion.
